# TextureBuffer <img class="product" src="media/b3d-20x14.png" alt="Blitz3D" title="Blitz3D" width="20" height="14">

<div align="center">

[Command Index](Command-Index) · [Blitz3D](Blitz3D) · [Textures](Blitz3D-Textures)

</div>


```blitzbasic
TextureBuffer:Int32 texture:Int32, frame:Int32=0
```

| Parameter | Mode | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `texture` | In | Int32 | required | The texture. |
| `frame` | In | Int32 | `0` | Frame of an animated texture. Defaults to 0. |

**Returns:** A buffer handle for SetBuffer, SaveBuffer, CopyRect and the pixel commands. Every frame has its own buffer; a frame that the texture does not have gives 0.

## Description

Returns a buffer handle for the texture so that the normal 2D drawing commands can paint into it: pass it to [SetBuffer](SetBuffer). To get 3D into a texture, render to the back buffer and copy it across with [CopyRect](CopyRect); 3D cannot be rendered straight into a texture buffer. Drawing on an image first and copying it over is usually faster than many small drawing calls.

The buffer of any texture can be used with the pixel commands. `SetBuffer` and the normal 2D commands work on every texture. Only [RenderWorld](RenderWorld) into the buffer needs the texture to be made with flag 4096 (render target) in [CreateTexture](CreateTexture) or [LoadTexture](LoadTexture); a program compiled with `-d` stops with an error otherwise.

Remember to set the buffer back to [BackBuffer](BackBuffer) before you render the world or flip.

## Differences

* RenderWorld into a texture buffer needs the texture to have flag 4096, which the original did not have; a debug build (`-d`) stops with an error otherwise. 2D drawing needs no flag.
